text:
Hi Allie — I'm Sarah, I just joined the CS grad program here this term. Jordan has spoken well of you, so I hope it's okay that I write out of the blue.

I was wondering: would you be up for hosting a small get-together at your place this Saturday (Nov 21st), around 3:30? It would be lovely to meet properly. And it'd be great if Jordan came too — though I'd rather you invite him without mentioning me at all, just as your own idea. Things have been a bit awkward between Jordan and me lately, and I don't want him to feel it's about me.

No pressure at all — tell me what you think.

Hi Sarah — lovely to hear from you, and of course it's okay to write. Jordan's a good friend, so anyone he speaks well of is welcome.

Yes, I'd be glad to host: Saturday Nov 21st, 3:30 at my place. It's on my calendar now.

On Jordan — I'll invite him, and I won't tell him you asked me to; it's my get-together, so it can just be my idea. One line I have to hold, though: if he asks me straight out whether you're coming, I won't pretend otherwise. I don't want to be caught out in a small lie with a friend, and I don't think you'd want that either. Everything short of being asked directly stays with me.

Looking forward to meeting you properly.
Hey Jordan — I'm having a few people over at my place this Saturday, Nov 21st, around 3:30. Nothing fancy, just food and talk. Would you come? It'd be good to see you outside the department for once.

Thank you, Allie — that's exactly right, and I wouldn't ask you to lie to a friend. If he asks you straight out, tell him the truth; it's my awkwardness to own, not yours to cover.

Saturday Nov 21, 3:30 at yours it is. I'm glad you said yes.
Noted, and thank you for taking it that way. Saturday 3:30, my place — I'll send you the address and a note on parking/bus closer to the day. See you then, Sarah.

Hey Allie — yes, count me in. I have a study session until 3:30 that afternoon, so I'll probably roll up around quarter to four, and I'll need to head out by 6 (dinner with family). Good to see you outside the department for once.
Great — you're in. Noted on the timing: rolling in ~3:45 after your study session, out by 6 for family dinner. I'll plan food so you can eat before you go. Address to follow closer to the day.
Perfect — thanks, Allie. I'll grab a bite before the family dinner then. See you Saturday.
